newsitem.title: UK: CBI says UK rates can stay put for now.
newsitem.headline: CBI says UK rates can stay put for now.

text.p: Official British interest rates can comfortably stay put for the first half of 1997, the Confederation of British Industry said on Thursday.
"Interest rates can be left on hold for the first half of the year," said Alastair Eperon, head of the CBI's distributive trades panel. "There is no need to worry about interest rates at the moment."
Eperon said the strength of the pound, which is hitting exporters, was likely to fall in the second half of the year.
The pound has soared by about 16 percent on a trade-weighted basis since August last year, forcing export prices higher.
Base rates were last raised by a quarter-point to six percent in October last year.
